hypotheses.justification: Use hbad.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq to obtain measurable t ⊆ s \ G with the same product measure. For each x, its section T is measurable by measurable_prodMk_left, lies inside the section S of s, and is disjoint from G. Thus hsection and ae_iff give (ν.restrict S) T = 0 by measure_mono. Measure.restrict_apply identifies this with ν T because T ⊆ S, without requiring S measurable. Measure.measure_prod_null then gives product measure zero for t, and measure_congr transfers this to s \ G. This works also for empty sections and zero measures.

Split on whether ν is s-finite. In the positive case, install that instance and use the original proof. Otherwise Measure.prod is zero by its definition, which explicitly uses zero when the second measure is not s-finite, so the conclusion is immediate. Alternatively, replace the use of measure_prod_null in the underlying proof by Measure.measure_prod_null_of_ae_null, which requires no s-finiteness.
